messages.subject: Montrave cue count example project
parts:
Good day,

I'm hoping to use the Montrave cue count data to see what happens when I use criteria other than AIC to select among models of the detection function (including different #s of adjustment terms).

In the example project, AIC is used to select the appropriate number of Hermite polynomial adjustment terms for the half normal model, and the model with only one term is selected. I fit models with the half normal key function and each of 0, 1, and 2 Hermite polynomial adjustment terms, but the results with one adjustment term don't match those from what I thought should be the same model from the example project ("half-normal hermite w 92.5" vs. "EH hn hp 1" in the analysis window below).  

I was able to duplicate the other models included in the example (uniform with 2 cosine adjustment terms, and hazard rate with no adjustment terms; see matching results in the analysis window below). 

I didn't change the data filter, or any of the constraints in the model definition, and I can't find any differences in the model definition other than manual vs. automatic selection of the # of adjustment terms.  

I do see differences in the log and results files:

When I fit the half normal model with exactly 1 Hermite polynomial adjustment term:
1) the log file doesn't include any warnings about constraints
2) The 2nd page of the results mentions bounds on the first parameter of the pdf.

messages.author: 9c6614a1b3d9e242
messages.subject: Re: Montrave cue count example project
parts:
Eric Rextad suggested that Distance was likely using the parameter estimate from model 1 (half normal with no adjustments) as the starting value when fitting the model with one adjustment term, and that when I did not specify starting values, the likelihood converged at a local rather than the global minimum.

Indeed, the help files under "Specifying the Model" point out that:  "One advantage of automatic forward or sequential selection is that the parameter estimates from the previous fit are used as starting values for the next model.  So, for example, the parameter estimates for the fit with 0 adjustment terms would be used as starting values when trying 1 adjustment term.  This helps the algorithm to converge."

When I use the parameter estimate from the half-normal model with no adjustments as the starting value when fitting the model with one adjustment term, my results match those in the example. In this case, it appears that the likelihood is not smooth and converges at different minima depending on the starting values.

Thanks Eric R!
-Eric H
